name: a_global_fx_metals
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Global, FX, metals.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
DXY, USD/JPY, EUR/USD; gold, silver, copper (price, % change); ECB, BoE, BoJ, PBoC actions and quotes; Europe/Asia index moves overnight into the brief date.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.

## **DXY** `[Macro / FX]`
- The dollar index was **101.88**, down **0.1%**, at the latest Reuters reading on Friday, October 2; it was headed for a **third consecutive weekly gain**. (Reuters, Oct 2; publish time not available)
- DXY was reported above **102.00** early Monday, up **0.3%** in the session, after recovering from the post-payrolls decline. (Newsquawk, Oct 5 10:42 ET)

## **EUR/USD** `[Macro / FX]`
- EUR/USD was **$1.1259**, up **0.16%**, on Friday, October 2. (Reuters, Oct 2; publish time not available)
- EUR/USD was reported near **$1.1185** on Monday, its lowest level since **May 2025**. (Amber Markets, Oct 5 05:13 ET)
- French fiscal concerns and a widening French-German government-bond spread were cited alongside the euro’s decline; the spread was reported near **130 basis points**, its widest since **2012**. (NordFX, Oct 5 03:28 ET)

## **USD/JPY** `[Macro / FX]`
- USD/JPY was **157.79**, down **0.18%**, on Friday, October 2. (Reuters, Oct 2; publish time not available)
- USD/JPY was **157.81**, down **0.15%**, in a later Friday Reuters reading. (Reuters, Oct 2; publish time not available)
- USD/JPY was reported at **157.98** on Monday, below **158.00**. (Amber Markets, Oct 5 05:13 ET)

## **Gold** `[Macro / Commodities]`
- Spot gold was **$4,135.68 per ounce**, down **1.01%**, in Friday trading. (Reuters, Oct 2; publish time not available)
- A separate Friday Reuters reading placed spot gold at **$4,181.59 per ounce** at **04:33 ET**; gold was down more than **2% for the week** at that time. (Reuters, Oct 2 04:33 ET)
- Gold was reported at **$4,137.36 per ounce** on Monday morning and later near **$4,140**. (Amber Markets, Oct 5 05:13 ET; NordFX, Oct 5 03:28 ET)

## **Silver** `[Macro / Commodities]`
- Spot silver was **$61.21 per ounce**, up **0.6%**, in Friday trading. (Reuters, Oct 2; publish time not available)
- Another Friday reading placed spot silver at **$60.17 per ounce**, down **1.1%**. (CNBC, Oct 2; publish time not available)
- Silver was reported at **$60.99 per ounce** on Monday morning. (Amber Markets, Oct 5 05:13 ET)

## **Copper** `[Macro / Commodities]`
- London Metal Exchange three-month copper was **$14,298.33 per metric ton**, up **0.2%**, on Friday. (Reuters, Oct 2; publish time not available)
- U.S. copper futures were **$5.57 per pound**, up **0.4%**, in the same Friday report. (Reuters, Oct 2; publish time not available)
- LME three-month copper was later reported at **$14,289 per metric ton**, up **0.32%**. (Morgan Downey Commodity News, Oct 2; publish time not available)

## **ECB / Euro area** `[Macro / Calendar]`

## **BoE / United Kingdom** `[Macro / Calendar]`

## **BoJ / Japan** `[Macro / Calendar]`
- Tokyo headline and core inflation were reported at their highest levels since **November 2025**, above the BoJ’s **2%** target, on Friday, October 2. (Investing.com, Oct 2; publish time not available)
- A BoJ September meeting summary was reported as not signaling an imminent rate hike. (Saxo, Oct 5 06:18 ET)
- Japanese Finance Minister **Katayama** said over the weekend that the foreign-exchange trend had “changed somewhat” since the joint FX-intervention announcement. (Newsquawk, Oct 5 10:42 ET)

## **PBoC / China** `[Macro / Calendar]`
- China was closed for **Golden Week** on Monday, October 5, with markets scheduled to return on **October 8**. (NordFX, Oct 5 03:28 ET)
- No new PBoC policy action or named PBoC official quote published within the specified window was identified in the gathered results.

## **Europe—overnight indexes** `[Macro / Equities]`
- On Friday, October 2, the **DAX** rose **1.2%**, the **STOXX Europe 600** rose **0.8%**, and the **FTSE 100** rose **0.3%**. (Saxo, Oct 5 06:18 ET)

## **Asia—overnight indexes** `[Macro / Equities]`
- Early Monday, the **Nikkei 225** was up approximately **1.8%**, the **TOPIX** was up **0.8%**, and the MSCI Asia-Pacific index was up approximately **0.4%**. (Saxo, Oct 5 06:18 ET)
- The **Hang Seng**, **ASX 200**, and **Straits Times Index** were trading while mainland China was closed for Golden Week. (Saxo, Oct 5 06:18 ET)
- A later Monday report placed the **Nikkei 225** near **69,700**, up approximately **2.1%**, and the **Hang Seng** near **23,850**, down approximately **0.5%**. (NordFX, Oct 5 03:28 ET)

## **U.S. reference markets** `[Macro / Equities]`
- On Friday, October 2, the **S&P 500** rose **0.73%** to **7,722.72**, the **Nasdaq 100** rose **1.00%** to **30,807.93**, and the **Dow Jones Industrial Average** rose **0.49%** to **51,176.96**. (Saxo, Oct 5 06:18 ET)
